descripcion_es: I like, I prefer, I think…: expressing basic likes and opinions.
resumen: Verbs and set phrases to say what you like and don't like, express preferences and give a simple opinion.

explicacion.texto: Unlike Spanish, in English the subject is the person: I like music (Spanish says “a mí me gusta la música”). After like, love, hate, enjoy and prefer comes a noun or an -ing verb (I enjoy cooking). Would like (a polite way of saying “want”) takes to + infinitive.

filas: to like a lot (es: gustar mucho)
to get pleasure from (activities) (es: disfrutar, gustar)
We enjoy walking in the mountains.
to not be bothered by (es: no importar)
to dislike very much / to be unable to bear (es: odiar / no soportar)
to be enthusiastic about, to like (es: tener afición a, gustar)
to be very interested in, to like (informal) (es: estar metido en, gustar)
My son is really into video games.
to want to know more about (es: interesarse por)
to like A more than B (es: preferir A a B)
I'd rather stay at home tonight.
I think it's a great idea.
I believe it is not true that… (es: No creo que…)
This is my view:… (es: En mi opinión,…)
In my opinion, the film is too long.
What is your opinion of…? (es: ¿Qué te parece…?)
What do you think of the new café?
giving a simple opinion (es: Es aburrido / genial / horrible)
agreeing with someone (es: Yo también / Yo tampoco)

items: I don't think + affirmative is more natural than I think + negative: I don't think it's true.
Prefer A to B; would rather A than B: I'd rather walk than drive.
Me neither answers a negative sentence: I don't like it. – Me neither.

ejemplos.frase: I really enjoy reading in bed before I go to sleep.
ejemplos.traduccion: Me encanta leer en la cama antes de dormirme.

ejemplos.frase: My parents can't stand loud music.
ejemplos.traduccion: Mis padres no soportan la música alta.

ejemplos.frase: I prefer the mountains to the beach.
ejemplos.traduccion: Prefiero la montaña a la playa.

ejemplos.frase: What do you think of the new mayor?
I'd rather take the train than drive.
ejemplos.traduccion: Prefiero coger el tren a conducir.

ejemplos.frase: I don't think this restaurant is very good.
ejemplos.traduccion: No creo que este restaurante sea muy bueno.

errores_hispanohablantes.nota: The subject is the person, and nouns used in a general sense do not take the.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: What do you think about? (¿Qué te parece?)
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: What do you think of it?
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: You have to say what: What do you think of/about + something.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: I don't like it. – Me too.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: I don't like it. – Me neither.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: In reply to a negative, say me neither.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with the correct form of the verb in brackets.
ejercicios.explicacion: The rule on the card applies: after like, love, hate, enjoy and prefer comes a noun or a verb, and after enjoy it is always -ing. The clue is the verb enjoy before the gap. Enjoy means “to get pleasure from” and, with really, it is like saying “I love it”. That is why the form is dancing, never to dance.
ejercicios.traduccion: Me encanta bailar en las bodas.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Enjoy does not take to + infinitive; it always takes -ing (a typical mistake on the card).
After enjoy you need the -ing form: dancing.
Spelling mistake: the final e is dropped when you add -ing, dancing.

glosario.significado: disfrutar de, pasarlo bien haciendo algo; va seguido de -ing

glosario.definicion_l: take in marriage; married · perform a marriage ceremony

ejercicios.explicacion: The structure prefer A to B (“to like A more than B”) applies. The clue is the verb prefer and the two -ing activities being compared. The preposition is to, which matches Spanish “a”. It is a common mistake to use than, as with comparatives, but prefer is not a comparative.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: To like A more than B is prefer A to B.
ejercicios.traduccion: Prefiero ir en bici a correr.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Than is used with comparatives (better than); with prefer, use to.
That does not introduce the second item of the preference; the preposition is to.
This copies other structures; the second item after prefer is introduced by to.

glosario.definicion_l: the sport of traveling on a bicycle or motorcycle

ejercicios.explicacion: The expression be interested in (“to want to know more about”) applies. The clue is interested before the gap. The fixed preposition is in, even though Spanish says “interesarse por”. It can be followed by a noun (modern art) or an -ing verb (interested in learning).
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: To want to know more about something is be interested in.

errores_previstos.explicacion: This is a word-for-word copy of Spanish “interesarse por”; the fixed preposition is in.
On goes with keen (keen on), not with interested.
Interested is not used with about; the preposition is in.

ejercicios.frase: I'd ___ stay at home than go to the party.
ejercicios.explicacion: The expression would rather + infinitive without to (“would prefer”) applies. The clue is I'd (short for I would) followed by stay without to, and the comparison with than go to the party. The missing word is rather. Unlike prefer, would rather does use than for the second item.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Would prefer is would rather + infinitive without to.
ejercicios.traduccion: Preferiría quedarme en casa antes que ir a la fiesta.

errores_previstos.explicacion: I'd prefer needs to before the verb (I'd prefer to stay) and is not combined with than like this; here the structure is would rather.
I'd better means “it is advisable for me to”; it does not express preference.
I'd like needs to + infinitive and does not take than: the structure is I'd rather.

glosario.significado: preferiría; va con infinitivo sin to y con than para el segundo término

ejercicios.frase: My brother isn't very keen ___ sport.
ejercicios.explicacion: The expression be keen on (“to be enthusiastic about”) applies. The clue is keen before the gap. The fixed preposition is on. In the negative, not very keen on is a mild and very British way of saying we don't like something.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Be keen on means to be enthusiastic about.
ejercicios.traduccion: A mi hermano no le gusta mucho el deporte.

por_opcion.on: Correct: be keen on is the fixed expression (“to be enthusiastic about”).
por_opcion.of: Incorrect: of goes with fond (be fond of), which has a similar meaning, but not with keen.
por_opcion.in: Incorrect: in goes with interested (be interested in), not with keen.

glosario.significado: ser aficionado a, tener afición a

ejercicios.explicacion: The rule on the card applies: would like (“to want, politely”) takes to + infinitive. The clue is I'd like, short for I would like, which expresses a specific wish, not a general liking. That is why the form is to see. Don't confuse it with like + -ing, which talks about habitual likes.
ejercicios.traduccion: Me gustaría ver la nueva exposición.

por_opcion.to see: Correct: would like + to + infinitive for a specific wish.
por_opcion.seeing: Incorrect: like + -ing expresses a general liking, but would like requires to + infinitive.
por_opcion.see: Incorrect: to is missing; would like is not used with the infinitive without to.

glosario.definicion_l: the act of exhibiting · a collection of things (goods or works of art etc.) for public display

ejercicios.explicacion: The rule on the card applies: to agree with a negative sentence, say Me neither. The clue is I don't like, which is negative. Spanish says “yo tampoco”, so the English reply must also be negative; Me too and So do I are only for affirmative sentences.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: To agree with a negative: me neither.
ejercicios.traduccion: No me gusta la comida picante. — A mí tampoco.

Correct: agreement with a negative sentence (es: a mí tampoco).
Incorrect: Me too answers an affirmative (es: a mí también); after a negative it is the typical mistake on the card.
Incorrect: it is an affirmative reply (es: yo también); for a negative it would be Neither do I.

glosario.definicion_l: producing a burning sensation on the taste nerves · suggestive of sexual impropriety

ejercicios.frase: I can't ___ people who talk during films.
ejercicios.explicacion: The expression can't stand (“to be unable to bear”) applies. The clue is can't before the gap and the clearly negative meaning of the sentence. In this expression stand means “to bear, to tolerate” and is only used like this in negatives or questions. It is stronger than don't like and roughly equivalent to hate.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: To be unable to bear something is can't stand.
ejercicios.traduccion: No soporto a la gente que habla durante las películas.

por_opcion.stand: Correct: can't stand means “to be unable to bear”.
por_opcion.mind: Incorrect: can't mind is not used; mind appears in don't mind (“it doesn't bother me”) and in questions such as Do you mind…?
por_opcion.enjoy: Incorrect: can't enjoy means “to be unable to enjoy”, not “to be unable to bear”, and makes no sense here.

glosario.significado: importar, molestar (don't mind = no me importa)

ejercicios.explicacion: The rule on the card applies: enjoy is followed by -ing, never by to + infinitive. The clue is enjoys to travel. Change to travel into travelling (with double l in British English) or traveling (in American English); that is why both spellings are accepted.
ejercicios.traduccion: A mi hermana le encanta viajar.

errores_previstos.explicacion: This leaves the sentence uncorrected: enjoy takes -ing.
This corrects the verb but loses the third-person -s: enjoys.
This mixes the two structures: after enjoy the -ing form comes directly, without to.

glosario.significado: disfrutar de, gustar mucho; va con -ing

ejercicios.frase: I would like visiting Rome next year.
respuestas: I would like to visit Rome next year.
I'd like to visit Rome next year.
ejercicios.explicacion: The rule on the card applies: would like is followed by to + infinitive. The clue is I would like followed by visiting. It is a specific wish (Rome, next year), not a general liking, so you must say to visit. Both the full form I would like and the contraction I'd like are accepted.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Would like is followed by to + infinitive.
ejercicios.traduccion: Me gustaría visitar Roma el año que viene.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I would like visiting Rome next year.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This leaves the sentence uncorrected: would like takes to + infinitive.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I would like visit Rome next year.
errores_previstos.explicacion: To is missing: would like to visit.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I like to visit Rome next year.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This loses would; I like expresses a general liking and does not fit with next year.

ejercicios.explicacion: The structure prefer A to B applies, together with the warning on the card that prefer takes to, not than. The clue is prefer followed by than. Although the sentence compares two things, prefer is not a comparative adjective, so the second item is introduced by to: I prefer coffee to tea.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: With prefer, use to, not than.

errores_previstos.explicacion: This leaves the sentence uncorrected: with prefer, use to.
That does not introduce the second item; the preposition is to.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I prefer the coffee to the tea.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Nouns used in a general sense do not take the, as the card reminds you.

respuestas: What do you think of it
ejercicios.explicacion: The phrase on the card What do you think of it? applies, used to ask for an opinion (es: ¿qué te parece?). The clue is the words what, do, you, think, of, it: the question needs do, and think of must be followed by the thing you are giving an opinion on (it). As the card points out, What do you think about? is not enough: you have to say about what.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: To ask for an opinion (es: ¿Qué te parece?): What do you think of it?

errores_previstos.respuesta: What you do think of it
errores_previstos.explicacion: In questions the auxiliary do goes before the subject: What do you think…

errores_previstos.respuesta: What do you think it of
errores_previstos.explicacion: The preposition goes before its object: think of it.

respuestas: My son is really into photography
ejercicios.explicacion: The informal expression be into (“to be very interested in”) applies. The clue is the words is and into, which form the expression, and the subject my son. The order is subject + is + really + into + object: really goes between the verb and into to intensify it. It is very common in spoken English.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Be into means to be very interested in something.
ejercicios.traduccion: A mi hijo le gusta muchísimo la fotografía.

errores_previstos.respuesta: My son is really photography into
errores_previstos.explicacion: Into is a preposition and goes before its object: into photography.

errores_previstos.respuesta: My son is into really photography
errores_previstos.explicacion: Really cannot go between the preposition and its object.

glosario.significado: ser aficionado a algo, encantarle algo (informal)

glosario.definicion_l: the act of taking and printing photographs · the process of producing images of objects on photosensitive surfaces

ejercicios.explicacion: The expression don't mind + -ing (“it doesn't bother me”) applies. The clue is the hint “it doesn't bother me” in the instruction, the structure I don't ___ and the -ing verb working after it. The word is mind. It is a neutral way of saying that something is not a problem, without going as far as saying you like it.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: To not be bothered by something is don't mind + -ing.
ejercicios.traduccion: No me importa trabajar los fines de semana.

errores_previstos.explicacion: I don't care means “it makes no difference to me, I'm not worried”, with a note of indifference; “I'm happy to (do it)” is I don't mind.
This is a word-for-word copy of Spanish “importar”; matter does not take the person as subject and is not used with -ing here.
Import means to bring goods in from abroad (the commercial sense of Spanish “importar”).

glosario.significado: no importar, no molestar hacer algo

ejercicios.explicacion: The vocabulary of likes on the card applies: favourite means “liked most of all” and goes before the noun. The clue is the question What's your ___ book?, the usual way of asking about a preference. Favourite is the British spelling; in American English it is written favorite.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Liked most of all is favourite (favorite in American English).

por_opcion.favourite: Correct: favourite (favorite in American English) is the normal adjective for “liked most of all”.
por_opcion.preferred: Incorrect in this context: preferred exists, but it is formal or technical (preferred method, preferred supplier) and is not used for personal likes.
por_opcion.liked: Incorrect: liked is a participle (a well-liked teacher) and is not used to mean “favourite”.

glosario.definicion_l: like better; value more highly · select as an alternative over another

descripcion_larga_es: This card brings together the verbs and set phrases for saying what you like and don't like (like, love, enjoy, hate, can't stand), expressing preferences (prefer, would rather) and giving a simple opinion. It is everyday vocabulary and appears in any conversation. Spanish speakers find it hard because in English the subject is the person (“I like”) and each verb requires its own structure.

contexto.que_es: It is the basic vocabulary of likes, preferences and opinions: verbs such as like, love, enjoy, hate, mind and can't stand; expressions such as be keen on, be into or be interested in; and phrases for preferring (prefer A to B, would rather) and for asking for or giving an opinion (What do you think of…?).
contexto.por_que_importa: Talking about yourself and reacting to what others say is the basis of any conversation and of the first parts of an oral exam. Each verb requires a specific structure (-ing, to + infinitive, a preposition), and getting it wrong is noticed at once. Also, short replies such as Me neither or So do I are essential to sound natural.
contexto.cuando_se_usa: It is used when introducing yourself, talking about hobbies, choosing between options or commenting on something you have seen or read. Spanish speakers often copy “me gusta” word for word (Me like), use than with prefer, put to after enjoy or reply Me too to a negative sentence, where English requires Me neither.
